comments.body: Fixed in commit 451212e377a with teenage-unquieted-ringworm's next-batch rebuild: blocker statuses now come from every ticket's reduced state, with error/fsck_needed and missing tickets counted as finished, matching ready. Tests: test_non_terminal_blocker_outside_the_active_set_still_blocks[blocked|idea] fail on the old code and pass on the new; test_closed_blocker_releases_its_dependent passes on both. On a clone of the live store, all 11 open epics give identical output, so no live ticket is currently affected.

compiled_state.description:
## Observation

`next_batch.compute` builds `ticket_status_map` only from `list_states(status="open,in_progress")` plus tombstones. `_open_blockers_by_ticket` then looks each blocker up with a default of `"closed"`. A blocker whose status is `blocked` or `idea` is missing from the map, so it reads as `closed` (terminal), and the ticket it blocks is offered as ready.

Reproduced at unit level on db9352e6da0. A is `blocked`; B is `open` and `depends_on` A.
- With next-batch's status map (`{"B": "open"}`): `_open_blockers_by_ticket` returns `{}`, so B is ready.
- With A's real status in the map: it returns `{"B": ["A"]}`.
- `is_terminal_status("blocked")` and `is_terminal_status("idea")` are both False.

`ready` (`graph/_ready.py`) gets this right: it checks every blocker's reduced status and treats only missing tickets as finished. So the two ops disagree on whether B is workable.

Unchecked: how many open tickets in the live store currently depend on a `blocked`/`idea` ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test where an open task under an epic depends on a `blocked` (and, separately, an `idea`) ticket shows next-batch reporting it as skipped-blocked, not batched.
- [ ] next-batch takes blocker status from the reduced state of every ticket, not from the open/in_progress list.
- [ ] The existing next-batch tests and the parity tests still pass.

## Plan
1. Add a failing test in `tests/unit/test_next_batch_*` (next to the existing next-batch tests): an epic with an open task that `depends_on` a `blocked` ticket, and a second case with an `idea` blocker. Assert the task lands in `skipped_blocked`, naming the blocker, and is absent from the batch.
2. In `src/rebar/_engine_support/next_batch.py`, build the blocker status map from the reduced state of every ticket (the whole-store pass `compute` already does), overlaid with tombstone status, instead of from `list_states(status="open,in_progress")`. This is the same rule `graph/_ready.py` applies: every blocker's real status, with a missing ticket counted as finished.
3. Run the existing next-batch tests and parity tests, then `make verify`.

This lands in the same change as the next-batch single-pass rebuild (teenage-unquieted-ringworm), which replaces the second whole-store read; the commit carries both tickets' trailers.

## File impact (expected)
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/next_batch.py`
- `tests/unit/` next-batch test module (located during step 1)
